svg.title: The flow Cedar – Dispatch watch
svg.desc: Top to bottom. Trigger: a work order is added or modified with FieldLink status or Urgent in the request, and the saved row is Sent, urgent and active. Three preparation actions: Settings parses the JSON environment variable, Wait minutes takes acceptanceCheckMinutes or 10, Initialize Checks sets a counter to zero. Do until loop named Wait for acceptance, limits count 3 and timeout two hours: Delay for the configured minutes, Read the work order selecting status and state, Count the check; the loop ends when the status is no longer Sent or the row is inactive. After the loop: Read final state, then a Compose named Outcome with one of five words. A Switch on Outcome: case silent runs Stamp the reminder, then two parallel branches, Add a note and a Condition (due within four hours: mail dispatch and the service manager, otherwise mail dispatch), then Reminder done after both. Case rejected: one Compose saying plug-in step R1 handles it. Default for moved, reminded and closed: nothing. Side notes: the flow listens to status and urgent and writes only the reminder stamp, so it cannot start itself; a second run for the same work order finds the stamp and ends as reminded.
svg.text: Cedar – Dispatch watch (C-38): wait, look again, decide once
Trigger: work order added or modified
Select columns: FieldLink status, Urgent · Filter rows: Sent, urgent, active
Settings (json of the environment variable) → Wait minutes → Initialize Checks = 0
Do until “Wait for acceptance” (Count 3, Timeout PT2H)
Delay n minutes
Read the work order
Count the check
until: status is not Sent, or the row is inactive
Read final state → Outcome = closed | silent | reminded | rejected | moved
Switch “By outcome”
Case 'silent'
Stamp the reminder
Add a note (no retry)
Condition: due within 4 hours?
True: mail dispatch + service manager
False: mail dispatch
Reminder done (after both)
Case 'rejected'
One Compose: plug-in step R1 already
creates the reassignment task (lesson 68).
Default: moved, reminded, closed
No action. The description on the default
says why.
Why it is built this way
Listens to status and Urgent, writes
only the reminder stamp: no self-start.
Body first, test after: even a work order
accepted at once gets one check.
Limit reached = loop Succeeded.
So the decision is taken on a fresh
read, not on how the loop ended.
Second run for the same work order:
finds the stamp, outcome 'reminded',
nothing is sent twice.
Depth 3. One counter, used by one loop.
